sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English podcast.
My name is Emily.
I'm happy you are here today.
In this episode, we will talk about Greece.
Greece is a beautiful and sunny country in Southern Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Greece?
Greece is in Southern Europe.
It is near the Mediterranean Sea.
It is next to Albania, North Macedonia, Bulgaria, and Turkey.
It has many islands in the sea.
Greece is part of the European Union.
It is a popular place for tourists.
What is the capital city of Greece?
The capital city is Athens.
Athens is a very old city.
People have lived there for thousands of years.
In Athens, you can visit the Acropolis and ancient hill with temples.
The most famous temple is called the Parthenon.
Athens is full of history, museums, shops, and cafes.
How many people live in Greece?
About 10 million people live in Greece.
Many people live in cities like Athens, Thessaloniki, and Patras.
Others live in villages, islands, or mountain areas.
There are more than 6,000 islands in Greece, but only about 200 are inhabited.
What language do people speak in Greece?
People in Greece speak Greek.
Greek is the official language.
It has a special alphabet different from the English alphabet.
Many Greek people also speak English, especially in cities and tourist areas.
What is the weather like in Greece?
Greece has a Mediterranean climate.
This means it has hot, dry summers, and mild wet winters.
In summer, the weather is very sunny and warm.
People go to the beach and swim in the sea.
In winter, it is cooler and rainy.
In the mountains, it sometimes snows.
What does Greece look like?
Greece has many mountains, islands, and beaches.
It also has beautiful blue water and white houses.
The land is rocky and dry, but there are olive trees and vineyards.
In the north, there are green forests and lakes.
The highest mountain in Greece is Mount Olympus.
In Greek mythology, it was the home of the gods.
What animals live in Greece?
In Greece, you can see goats, sheep, foxes, and turtles.
In the sea, there are dolphins, fish, and sea turtles.
In the mountains, there are eagles, owls, and other birds.
Greece also has many cats, especially in villages and on islands.
What do people eat in Greece?
Greek food is healthy and tasty.
It uses olive oil, vegetables, cheese, and seafood.
Some popular foods are Greek salad with tomatoes, cucumber,
onion, olives, and feta cheese.
Musaka, baked dish with eggplant, meat, and cream sauce.
Suvlaki, grilled meat on a stick, satsiki, yogurt with cucumber and garlic.
Baklava, sweet dessert with nuts and honey, people also eat bread, rice, fish, and fruit.
What is life like in Greece?
Life in Greece is relaxed.
People enjoy spending time with family and friends.
They often sit outside, talk, and drink coffee or cold drinks.
People go to the market, cook fresh food, and take a rest in the afternoon.
Many people work in tourism, farming, or fishing.
Others work in schools, offices, or shops.
In summer, families go to the islands or villages to rest and enjoy the sea.
What are some Greek traditions and holidays?
Easter is the most important holiday in Greece.
People go to church, eat lamb, and celebrate with fireworks.
August 15 is a big holiday, the day of the Virgin Mary.
Name days are also important.
People celebrate the day of the saint they are named after.
There are many festivals with music, dance, and food, especially in summer.
Traditional Greek dancing is fast and fun.
People hold hands and dance in circles.
Some fun facts about Greece.
Greece is the birthplace of democracy and the Olympic Games.
The Greek flag is blue and white.
The Greek alphabet has 24 letters.
Greece has more than 18 UNESCO World Heritage sites.
The sea around Greece is very blue and clear.
The Greek word for hello is yassas.
Now you know many things about Greece.
You know where it is, what people speak, and what the weather is like.
You learned about Greek food, culture, and daily life.
Good job!
I am Emili.
Goodbye, or as they say in Greek, yassas.
